Draw deaths as a Bernoulli/Poisson count

Source: R/utils.R
binomial_from_poisson.Rd

The alternative mortality draw, selected with createProcess(mortality_draw = "poisson"). The default since 0.2.0 is mortality_draw = "binomial", the exact binomial; binomial_from_gamma() (mortality_draw = "gamma") reproduces results published before 0.2.0. A cohort of one tree or fewer (n <= 1.5) is a Bernoulli trial and is drawn as one; every larger cohort is drawn from a Poisson capped at n.

Usage

binomial_from_poisson(n, p)

Arguments

n

torch.Tensor Number of trees at risk per cohort.

p

torch.Tensor Annual mortality probability per cohort.

Value

A torch tensor of integer death counts, never exceeding n.

Details

binomial_from_gamma() matches a Gamma to the binomial's first two moments and rsample()s it, which buys a pathwise gradient – the hazard it guards against is a discrete draw having no gradient at all. The forward pass then rounds that draw straight-through (finn-class.R), so the gradient flows through a quantity the simulation discards, and the rounded count delivers a measured 0.68-0.72 of the calibrated deaths for one-tree cohorts at annual probabilities of 0.01-0.10 (5e5 draws per probability; 0.76 at p = 0.26). This draw is integer-valued, exact in expectation for small n*p, and carries no pathwise gradient, which is how Lin et al. (2026) treat discrete events in a differentiable crop model: resolve them before differentiation and hold them fixed during gradient evaluation. The Bernoulli branch is not cosmetic – capping a Poisson at a one-tree cohort delivers only 88\ suppressed stem, which is the stem that decides thinning.

The choice shows up in the simulated stand rather than in a holdout score: a long simulation to equilibrium separates the two draws by a factor of several in basal area and stem number, while the fitted loss moves far less, because the rounded deficit is a bias on the trajectory and not on the parameters.

References

Lin et al. (2026). doi:10.48550/arXiv.2610.36827

See also

binomial_from_gamma(), binomial_from_bernoulli(), createProcess() (mortality_draw)

Examples

FINN.seed(1)
# cohorts of one tree are Bernoulli trials, larger cohorts a capped Poisson
n <- torch::torch_tensor(rep(c(1, 40), each = 10000))
p <- torch::torch_full(c(20000), 0.1)
d <- as.numeric(binomial_from_poisson(n, p))
# mean deaths per cohort: expected 0.1 (one tree) and 4 (forty trees)
tapply(d, rep(c("n = 1", "n = 40"), each = 10000), mean)
#>  n = 1 n = 40 
#> 0.1009 4.0245 
range(d)   # whole trees, and never more than the cohort holds
#> [1]  0 13
